answer: Clock-skew device fingerprinting resists sybils: every physical host's crystal oscillator drifts at a minute, manufacturing-unique rate readable from TCP timestamps. Like a prism fanning white light into fixed bands, skew analysis spreads an ocean of agents into a spectrum of distinct drift signatures, so a thousand clones sharing one machine collapse onto a single line. Temperature bends the rate, a node humming in frozen tundra reading differently from a warm datacenter, so forging N seats means running N physically separate boxes, each a real oscillator you cannot clone in software.
